subject: Security exhibit — inspection model selection and evidence turnover steps
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novumhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procureops@novumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit — evidence cadence question

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for sending through the draft exhibit (attached). Two quick things from our procurement and security teams:

1) Inspection model: our baseline requirement is the right to audit / inspection for SOC 2 scope items. We're evaluating whether we want a continuous inspection clause (on-demand access + live sampling) vs. a bounded sampling model (scheduled windows + defined sample sets). The continuous approach is attractive for us from a risk perspective but operationally heavy for vendors.

2) Evidence cadence: if we go bounded sampling, what's a realistic weekly/monthly evidence handover we can expect (assertions, changed controls, test scripts, system screenshots, limited logs)? If continuous, what are safe operational guardrails (ephemeral access, notice windows, rate limits)?

Can you outline Redwood's preferred default and any guardrails you need so we can align and move order-form redlines forward?

Attaching the Novum side security checklist for reference.

Appreciate a short summary and recommended language we can add to the order form.

Regards,
Alex Chen
Head of Information Security — NovumHealth

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novumhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — evidence cadence question

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for the checklist. Short answer up-front: Redwood recommends bounded sampling as the default inspection model with a defined pen-test cadence and an ephemeral-access process for time-boxed investigations. That approach balances your need for assurance with operational stability for running production inference.

High-level proposal:
- Inspection model: bounded sampling (30-day scheduling windows, up to 2 inspection windows per rolling 12 months; sample sets mutually agreed in advance).
- Pen test: mutual 30–60 day notice, vendor-approved third-party tester allowed, staging access via ephemeral credentials, coordinated blast radius (no noisy load tests against prod unless explicitly agreed).
- Evidence cadence (bounded model):
  - Monthly bundle: SOC 2 attestations, control-mapping spreadsheet, summary of configuration drift items (if any).
  - Pre-inspection: 10 business days pre-window evidence handover (exported artifacts + short walkthrough).
  - On-inspection: scoped ephemeral access (read-only console views, audit logs limited to sampled services).
- Operational guardrails for on-demand/continuous requests: minimum 14 business days advance notice, max 8 hours of interactive access per month unless escalation approved by Redwood Security.

Why bounded by default: continuous inspection has material overhead on secure multi-tenant services (risk of exposing operational telemetry and higher customer impact). Bounded sampling + strong pen-test process gives equivalent assurance for most enterprise customers and is what we include in our standard order form.

Action items I propose:
- Laura and Kim: can you take a pass on order-form language that captures the bounded model + optional continuous carve-out for regulated customers (with premium pricing / dedicated capacity)?
- Alex/Sanjay: confirm whether Novum needs continuous as a hard requirement or if a bounded + 2x annual pen-test package is acceptable. If acceptable, we'll circulate a redline.

I'm attaching Redwood's suggested exhibit template and the current order-form redlines.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Folks — looping in Legal / Compliance notes.

Quoted for context:
On Wed, 30 Sep 2026 at 10:05, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear ask ... Redwood recommends bounded sampling as the default inspection model ...

Suggested redline summary (high level):
1) Inspection scope: limit to mutually agreed SOC 2 system boundaries and assertions; require Novum to submit a sampling request 15 business days before window start; Redwood to return an evidence package 7 business days before the window (control mapping, exported config snapshots, relevant sanitized logs).
2) Access model: we will provide ephemeral, read-only access to staging or sanitized telemetry; privileged access to production is not provided. For any production-level deep-dive, a scoped forensic review will be run with a Redwood engineer present and under an agreed statement of work.
3) Pen test language: allow customer-provided third-party testers with standard safety clauses (no active exploit chains, pre-approved test plan, blast-radius limits); require 30 day notice; tests to be run against a customer-dedicated staging environment unless customer purchases dedicated capacity.
4) Evidence retention/exports: Redwood will retain audit artifacts for 90 days by default; customers may request longer retention as an add-on (to be priced).
5) Escalation: for findings that indicate an uncovered production vulnerability, Redwood will provide a remediation plan within 10 business days and schedule a triage call within 3 business days of discovery.

I will prepare a tracked-redline doc for the Security Exhibit and a matching order-form clause that captures: bounded sampling default, optional continuous carve-out (requires dedicated capacity add-on), pen-test workflow, evidence handover timelines, and retention opt-ins.

Attaching the initial redline and the order-form snippet for review: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Redline_20260930.docx (redline)

Laura — any further commercial caveats?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Redline_20260930.docx (DOCX)]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novumhealth.com>

Mateo / Kim / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the candid trade-offs. Novum's procurement and security teams reviewed the bounded-model proposal and the redline draft you attached. We are comfortable with bounded sampling as the default if two items are clarified:

1) Retention: please confirm the 90-day retention is for raw artifacts/exports; can we have a 12-month retention option for control-mapping exports (we can pay for an add-on)?
2) Order-form language: please add explicit language that if Novum escalates to continuous inspection for regulatory reasons, Redwood will propose a capability/pricing path and timeline (not an automatic denial).

If you can confirm those two points and circulate the redline with the minor edits, Novum will sign the order form and we can lock in the first pen-test window (targeting early Q1 2027).

Action items going forward:
- Redwood to update redline with retention add-on clause & continuous-inspection path. (Kimberly)
- Redwood to provide a mutual action plan (MAP) with dates for: order-form sign, pen-test contract, and pre-inspection evidence handover. (Mateo)
- Novum to confirm preferred pen-test vendor and provide preliminary dates by 2026-10-14. (Alex/Sanjay)

Appreciate the partnership — if we can get a MAP by next week we'll lock in the timeline.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of Information Security — NovumHealth
